outcome: GA-012: a release on the Release Owner's coverage exception is in force as closed in every lane, so the owner merges and record-release records it, as the Coverage is mandatory constraint already says. The branch also carries PR #348's review record.
acceptance_criteria: GA-012.1. `lane_in_force(release_lane, target, coverage_exception)` returns `closed` when `coverage_exception` holds words, whatever `release_lane` and `target` say. An exception is recorded only when coverage isn't `checked` (as `coverage_line` does today), so an exception passed with checked coverage isn't recorded and changes nothing. Otherwise it returns what it returns today. `release_lane` itself never moves.

GA-012.2. `release` with `--coverage-exception` and coverage not `checked` writes the handoff with `lane_in_force` `closed` and the exception's words and time. When `release_lane` is `wide`, its other gates still hold: an open failure in the ledger, links that aren't verified, or an open unknown needing the repository still refuses, naming each. Coverage is the only wide gate the exception answers.

GA-012.3. That handoff's instruction says coverage wasn't checked, quotes the exception, says DR-113 doesn't apply and the agent doesn't merge, and says the Release Owner merges under their own login. *Coverage is mandatory* has the owner make that merge, so a merge-instruction doesn't open it to the agent.

GA-012.4. `record-release` reads the exception from the handoff and computes the lane in force through `lane_in_force`. The Release Owner's merge is `human_merge_recorded`. Any agent merge of an exception handoff, with or without a merge-instruction, is `agent_merge_out_of_lane`. No outcome is added to the vocabulary. The record carries the handoff's `coverage` object as `release` wrote it, so the exception appears exactly when one was recorded.
GA-012.5. Without `--coverage-exception`, every lane behaves as it does today, and the wide lane still refuses on "coverage was not checked".
GA-012.6. `/gstack-build` Step 6 and `GOVERNANCE.md` each gain one sentence saying a coverage exception closes the lane for that release and the owner merges.

GA-012.7. Tests in `test_governed_review.py`: a wide-lane release with an exception writes a handoff in force as `closed` that carries the words; the same release with an open ledger failure refuses and names it; a contained-lane release with an exception is in force as `closed`; a closed lane deferred into `goal/g1` with an exception is in force as `closed`; a wide-lane release without an exception refuses as today; `record-release` records the owner's merge of an exception handoff as `human_merge_recorded` and an agent merge of one as `agent_merge_out_of_lane`, with a merge-instruction posted and without one.

GA-012.8. `gstack-execution` moves 0.104.1 to 0.105.0 in `plugin.json`, its marketplace entry and its README Version History, and the top-level marketplace version moves (CI-002). In CI, `run_all_tests.py` names `test_governed_review.py` among what it ran and reports no failures.

Docs: one sentence each in gstack-build Step 6 and GOVERNANCE.md. Seven tests.

links_introduced.links_introduced: the release handoff's `coverage.exception` (the Release Owner's words and the time they were recorded) becomes an input to `lane_in_force`. The reader's assumption is that a handoff carrying an exception was released by the Release Owner's merge, not the agent's. That holds because `release` and `record-release` both compute the lane in force from the handoff through `lane_in_force`, its one home, and a handoff with an exception is in force as `closed`.
